items.description: People should be free to make their own economic decisions with minimal government interference.
A strong social safety net ensuring no one falls into poverty or loses healthcare.
Private markets allocate resources better than government planning.
Government should actively correct market failures and reduce inequality.
Private property is a foundational right that should rarely be overridden.
Shared resources like parks, transit, and utilities should be publicly owned.
Decisions should be made at the most local level possible — neighborhood or city.
Uniform standards across the country ensure fairness and efficiency.
Citizens should vote directly on major policy questions.
Complex policy questions are best decided by trained specialists.
When problems are urgent, bold swift action beats careful deliberation.
Thorough debate and consensus-building produce better long-term outcomes.
Existing institutions deserve deference — they embody accumulated wisdom.
Current institutions are flawed and need significant structural change.
Individuals have a strong right to privacy from surveillance and data collection.
Monitoring and open data improve safety and hold people accountable.
Personal freedoms should be protected even when they conflict with group goals.
Shared norms and mutual obligation make societies function.
Rewards should flow to effort and ability, not identity or circumstance.
When groups systematically differ, policy should actively level the playing field.
Long-standing customs and values should be preserved across generations.
Society should continuously evolve toward new and better arrangements.
Criminal justice should focus on reintegrating offenders, not punishing them.
Clear consequences for rule-breaking deter harm and uphold justice.
Ecosystems and climate stability should be preserved even at economic cost.
Growth and jobs are essential — environmental costs are often overstated.
When harms are uncertain but potentially severe, restrict first and study later.
New technologies solve problems faster than regulation — let them develop.
People should move freely across borders; migration enriches everyone.
Countries have a right to control who enters and on what terms.
Major problems require international institutions and binding agreements.
Countries should prioritize their own capacity and avoid external dependencies.
Government operations should be maximally open and auditable by the public.
Some government functions require confidentiality to work effectively.
How individuals vote should remain secret to protect them from coercion.
Representatives' positions and votes should be fully visible to constituents.
